issues.legal_issue: An accused who participated in an assault may be convicted of grievous hurt rather than culpable homicide when the evidence does not reliably connect that accused’s blow to the fatal injury.
material_facts: The courts below found that the appellant assaulted the deceased and that injuries from the assault caused the deceased’s death.
The evidence was general and did not reliably connect the appellant’s blow to the internal injury that caused death.

The High Court had convicted the appellant under Section 304, Part II, IPC. The prosecution accepted that Section 325, read with Section 34, IPC, was the appropriate provision if the fatal injury could not be attributed to the appellant.
The other accused had not been convicted under Section 325, and the prosecution had not appealed against their convictions.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the conviction under Section 304, Part II, IPC, and convicted the appellant under Section 325, IPC; it did not alter the convictions of the other accused.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Sections 304, Part II, and 325, IPC, the Court held on these facts that the appellant’s participation in the assault supported a conviction for grievous hurt, but the evidence did not support attributing the fatal injury to him so as to sustain the culpable-homicide conviction. Section 34, IPC, was raised in relation to the proposed conviction, but the Court convicted this appellant under Section 325 alone because the other accused had not been convicted under that provision and no prosecution appeal was before it. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The accused appealed against a conviction arising from an assault.
predicates.appellant_assaulted_deceased: The evidence accepted by the court established that the accused assaulted the deceased.
predicates.evidence_does_not_attribute_fatal_injury: The evidence did not reliably connect the accused’s blow to the injury that caused the deceased’s death.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a conviction, the evidence establishes that the accused assaulted the deceased, and the fatal injury cannot reliably be attributed to that accused, the rule substitutes a grievous-hurt conviction for a culpable-homicide conviction.

issues.legal_issue: A sentence may be confined to the imprisonment already undergone when that punishment is adequate in light of the circumstances, including the offender’s rehabilitation.
material_facts: The appellant had already undergone a substantial period of imprisonment as an undertrial prisoner and as a convict.
After being released on bail, the appellant had established a typing institute and settled into life.
The Court considered that returning him to prison at that late stage would serve no useful purpose.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the imprisonment already undergone was adequate and confined the sentence for the grievous-hurt offence to that period.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its sentencing judgment in light of the punishment already undergone, the appellant’s rehabilitation, and the view that further imprisonment would serve no useful purpose. No specific sentencing provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction and substantial_sentence_already_served and offender_rehabilitated and further_imprisonment_serves_no_useful_purpose

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The offender appealed against a conviction and sentence.
predicates.substantial_sentence_already_served: The offender had already undergone a substantial period of imprisonment for the case.
predicates.offender_rehabilitated: After release, the offender had established a livelihood and settled into life.
predicates.further_imprisonment_serves_no_useful_pu: The court considered that sending the offender back to prison would serve no useful purpose.

issues.definition: When an offender appealing a conviction has already served a substantial sentence, has rehabilitated, and further imprisonment would serve no useful purpose, the sentence may be confined to the time already served.

issues.legal_issue: An admitted house trespass supported upholding the conviction for the house-trespass offence.
material_facts: The appellant’s house trespass was admitted.
The appeal also challenged the conviction under Section 449, IPC.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the conviction under Section 449, IPC, as justified by the admitted house trespass.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 449, IPC, and held that the conviction was justified because house trespass was admitted. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The accused appealed against a conviction that included a house-trespass offence.
predicates.house_trespass_admitted: The accused admitted that house trespass had occurred.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a house-trespass conviction and the house trespass is admitted, the conviction is upheld.
